title: Module review
subtitle: Everything from The Vineyard
objectives: Explain how the grape and the vine's year shape wine
Describe the effects of climate, soil and site

steps.prompt: Put the vine's yearly stages in order.
steps.explanation: Buds, flowers, berries, colour change and then the harvest.

steps.prompt: Match each factor to its effect.
steps.explanation: Each of these changes the temperature and so the ripening.

steps.prompt: What does the skin of a black grape mainly give the wine?
steps.explanation: Skins hold most of the colour, tannin and aroma; pulp holds sugar, acid and water.

steps.prompt: Very fertile soils usually give the best quality grapes.
steps.explanation: Not true. Fertile soils push the vine to grow leaves. Poorer, well-drained soils focus it on the fruit.

steps.prompt: Which choices tend to increase concentration in the fruit?
steps.explanation: Lower yields, removing bunches and mild stress all help. Heavy irrigation dilutes.

steps.title: What you learned
points: Skins give colour, tannin and aroma; small berries concentrate them
Climate sets the grape; weather sets the vintage
Soil, slope and altitude shape heat and water
Yield, canopy and picking date are the grower's key decisions
